newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bonn upper house wants ban on sheep, goat imports.
newsitem.headline: Bonn upper house wants ban on sheep, goat imports.

text.p: The German upper house of parliament asked the government on Friday to toughen an existing import ban on sheep and goat meat from Britain to protect consumers from scrapie, an illness related to mad cow disease, or BSE.
Germany currently bans imports of meat from sheep and goats that are over 12 months old and which contains brain, spinal cord or eyes.

But the Bundesrat said this was not sufficient to protect consumers. Because of the "high potential risk", it said it wanted the government to ban all imports of British sheep and goat meat and extend the existing ban on live imports.
Sheep have long been known to suffer from scrapie, a widespread brain-wasting disease similar to BSE.
The European Commission called a meeting of senior EU veterinary officials for Friday to review plans to ban the use of suspect sheep tissue in human and animal food.
Germany has been at the forefront of measures to restrict the export of British beef to stop brain-wasting bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) spreading to humans.

Its ban on sheep products was a protective measure based on scientific evidence that the fatal human equivalent of BSE, Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD), might be transferable to humans from sheep, the Health Ministry said last month.

The Bundesrat cannot force the government to make policy but is nevertheless influential because it represents the 16 federal states which are responsible for implementing bans on agricultural products.
British scientists said this week they had found more evidence that mad cow disease, most prevalent in Britain, could spread to people.
